motion: We should ban smartphones in elementary schools.
note: S帯を狙った強いPMスピーチ。比較の理由づけ・重要性・複数理由・固有例・一般化例・キーワード固有性・明確なサインポストを含む。
transcript: Ladies and gentlemen, hello everyone. Today's motion is that we should ban smartphones in elementary schools. As the Prime Minister, I will define this motion and present two points. By this motion we mean that children in elementary schools, from grade one to grade six, cannot bring smartphones into the school building; parents can still give them phones outside school. We have two points: first, protecting children's concentration and learning; second, protecting children from online dangers. Let me explain our first point: protecting concentration and learning. Elementary school children are six to twelve years old. Their brains are still developing, and unlike high school students or adults, they cannot yet control the urge to check notifications. Here is the key difference between our two sides: on the opposition side, smartphones stay in classrooms, and every buzz pulls a child's attention away from the teacher; on our side, the government side, the classroom is completely free from this distraction. Imagine a fourth-grade girl, Yuki, sitting in math class. Her phone vibrates with a game notification. She checks it under her desk, misses the explanation of fractions, and from that day math becomes something she does not understand. This is not a rare story; teachers across Japan report collecting phones during lessons every single week. There are two reasons this point matters. First, elementary school is where the foundation of all later learning is built. If children lose concentration in these six years, they cannot simply recover it in junior high. Second, unlike adults, children cannot choose their environment, so schools must choose it for them. This is exactly why the ban must happen at elementary schools specifically, not at high schools or workplaces: the younger the child, the weaker the self-control, and the more the school must protect them. Our second point is protecting children from online dangers. With smartphones at school, children can access social media during breaks without any adult supervision. Cyberbullying happens in group chats during lunch time, where no teacher can see it. For example, many bullying cases now start with a message sent at school and continue at home all night. When phones are banned at school, at least half of a child's day is safe, and bullies lose their main tool during school hours. To summarize why point one is our core argument: concentration is the foundation of elementary education, children cannot protect it by themselves, and only a school-level ban, not individual family rules, creates a classroom where every child can focus equally. For these two reasons, protecting learning and protecting safety, we are proud to propose this motion. Thank you.
